visibleObservations: Original is a readable quarter-turn conveyor: broad coral rails, blue-gray radial deck slats, warm wood frame and legs. Forms and color blocks are plain; side planes/legs fall very dark, especially beside the honey-wood approved straight family.

Fixed target supplies fuller, softly rounded rail volume, long warm edge reflections, layered slate slats and honey wood supports with restrained brass fasteners. It keeps the original palette family and functional identity. Native reconstruction may improve forms and construction rather than merely recolor the old parts.
Target end-plane bevels/framing are aesthetic drift: copying rounded or capped connection ends would damage modular joins. Target framing, physical scale and registration are not evidence.

Approved family native S is more restrained than the large target, but establishes the required continuous coral/slate/honey material vocabulary. The two supplied family PNGs are byte-identical approved native captures, not a second ImageGen target.

All96 original frames were inspected through four labeled contact sheets. The radial slat pattern changes throughout each facing; no missing facing or frame was found. This establishes baseline visibility, not new candidate acceptance.

Current catalog phone study preserves the right-angle path and a separate salmon plate over the deck. The old corner remains darker/flatter than the refined family straight modules. Repeated3×3 corners are a spacing/overlap study, not a valid directed continuous route.

deck.UV: u(q)=q*pi/4+(1-pi/4)*(3*q*q-2*q*q*q), q in[0,1]; v runs across deck. Incoming u0 and outgoing u1. Endpoint centerline derivative matches straight travel; interior angular phase deliberately compressed.

crossSections.note: At outgoing plane the across-section coordinate is Y; at incoming it is X. Curved interior must supply equivalent local across-section coordinates for shared shading.
